title: Microsoft Purview: DLP inline protection for more unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap dates, licensing, controls and documented browser behaviour are supported. One minor correction remains: the rollout checklist names simulation mode, but the controls table does not cover that setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans expanded browser inline protection for unmanaged generative AI apps in Edge for Business through Purview collection and DLP policies.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview collection and data loss prevention (DLP) policies will support browser inline protection for a significantly broader set of unmanaged generative AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Administrators can use existing Purview policy experiences to detect and protect sensitive data in supported browser activities.
claims.quote: Admins can use existing Purview policy experiences to detect and protect sensitive data shared through supported browser activities, helping extend consistent data security controls across more destinations.

claims.claim: Edge for Business enforces Purview DLP inline.
claims.quote: With a DLP policy, admins can apply inline data protection to identify, audit, and protect sensitive data in interactions with cloud apps (unmanaged and managed) in Microsoft Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Policies targeting unmanaged apps are supported on Windows 10 desktop devices.
claims.quote: DLP policies that target unmanaged apps in the browser apply to Microsoft Edge for Business on Windows 10 and Windows 11 desktop devices managed by Microsoft Intune.

claims.claim: Policies targeting unmanaged apps are supported on Windows 11 desktop devices.
claims.quote: DLP policies that target unmanaged apps in the browser apply to Microsoft Edge for Business on Windows 10 and Windows 11 desktop devices managed by Microsoft Intune.

claims.claim: These unmanaged-app policies apply on devices managed by Microsoft Intune.
claims.quote: You can use policies for unmanaged cloud apps in Edge for Business on Intune-managed devices

claims.claim: Unmanaged-app policies apply across all Edge browser profiles.
claims.quote: Policies targeting unmanaged apps on managed devices apply across all Edge browser profiles (work profile, personal profile and InPrivate).

claims.claim: ChatGPT consumer is a currently supported unmanaged app.
claims.quote: Browser policies in Edge for Business support these unmanaged apps: ... ChatGPT (consumer)

claims.claim: Google Gemini is a currently supported unmanaged app.
claims.quote: Browser policies in Edge for Business support these unmanaged apps: ... Google Gemini

claims.claim: DeepSeek is a currently supported unmanaged app.
claims.quote: Browser policies in Edge for Business support these unmanaged apps: ... DeepSeek

claims.claim: Perplexity AI is a currently supported unmanaged app.
claims.quote: Browser policies in Edge for Business support these unmanaged apps: ... Perplexity AI

claims.claim: The Purview portal path reaches All unmanaged AI apps and the Edge for Business enforcement choice.
claims.quote: Select Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. Select Inline web traffic. Select Custom ... Custom policy ... + Add cloud apps > Adaptive app scopes ... All unmanaged AI apps ... On the Choose where to enforce the policy step, select Edge for Business.

claims.claim: Adaptive app scopes apply only to supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.
claims.quote: Not all unmanaged AI apps are supported in Edge for Business. Adaptive app scopes apply only to the supported unmanaged AI apps in Edge for Business.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Saving the first qualifying policy causes Edge management service to create Edge configuration policies automatically.
claims.quote: After you save your first Purview collection or DLP policy targeting unmanaged apps in Edge for Business, the Microsoft Edge management service automatically creates the required Edge configuration policies, Microsoft Intune policies, and security groups

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The first qualifying policy also triggers automatic creation of Intune policies outside Purview.
claims.quote: When you activate a Microsoft Purview DLP policy for unmanaged cloud apps, Purview automatically creates the required Microsoft Edge configuration policies and Microsoft Intune policies (outside of Purview) and assigns the included users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The first qualifying policy also triggers automatic creation of security groups.
claims.quote: the Microsoft Edge management service automatically creates the required Edge configuration policies, Microsoft Intune policies, and security groups needed to activate the policy in the browser and prevent circumvention.

claims.claim: Two security groups are created automatically.
claims.quote: 2 security groups are created — one for included users and one for excluded users — that match the scope of your Purview policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: The automatically created Edge and Intune policies are read-only and are changed through Purview policy updates.
claims.quote: Automatically created policies are read-only and are updated automatically by making updates to the policies in Purview.

claims.claim: The auto-created policies and security groups update automatically when Purview policies change.
claims.quote: Once initially created, these policies and groups stay in sync and update automatically when changes are made to the Purview policies

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: A block policy prevents scoped users from using unprotected browsers where the policy does not apply.
claims.quote: If you configure the DLP policy to block, users in scope can't use unprotected browsers where the policy doesn't apply.

claims.claim: Firefox and other browsers are blocked for users subject to these block settings.
claims.quote: In Firefox and other browsers: Use of these browsers is blocked.

claims.claim: Chrome may remain usable, but a set list of unmanaged generative AI apps is blocked.
claims.quote: In Chrome browser: Use of the browser might be allowed depending on policy scope. If allowed, access to a set list of unmanaged generative AI apps is blocked.

claims.claim: The restriction on unprotected browsers does not affect the Edge for Business experience.
claims.quote: This restriction doesn't affect their experience in Microsoft Edge for Business.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Purview displays an error if automatic configuration sync fails.
claims.quote: If the automatic behaviors fail to sync, Microsoft Purview shows an error message.

claims.claim: A sync failure prevents enforcement in Edge for Business until an appropriately permitted administrator resyncs to resolve it.
claims.quote: Purview doesn’t enforce DLP and collection policies for unmanaged apps in Edge for Business until you resolve the error. An admin with the required permissions must resync to resolve the error.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP policies take priority over inline DLP policies when user, context and action match.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP policies are prioritized over inline DLP policies for cloud apps in Edge for Business if the same user, context, and action are configured in both policies.

claims.claim: Detection uses destination-app traffic, which may differ from the originating app.
claims.quote: When you target an unmanaged cloud app in an Edge for Business browser policy, detection is based on the destination app's traffic, which isn't always exactly the same as the originating app.

claims.claim: Encoded content or dynamic endpoints used intermittently by ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI may affect enforcement.
claims.quote: Some unmanaged AI apps like ChatGPT, Runway and Meta AI might intermittently send content in encoded form or through dynamically generated endpoints, which can impact policy enforcement.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation covers up to 4 MB for uploadText.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.

claims.claim: Inline evaluation supports files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.
claims.quote: Inline evaluation size limits: Microsoft Purview evaluates up to 4 MB of content for uploadText, and files up to 3 MB for uploadFile.

claims.claim: Purview browser and network data security policies do not apply to B2B guests.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview browser and network data security policies don't apply to B2B guest users.

claims.claim: An unmanaged-app policy can capture consumer and enterprise interactions sharing an app URL, including ChatGPT.
claims.quote: Policies that target unmanaged apps can capture interactions from both the consumer and enterprise versions of an app when the app's URL is shared across instances (for example, ChatGPT consumer and ChatGPT enterprise).

claims.claim: Inline protection for unmanaged apps does not support tenants using Intune multi-admin approval.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -EnforcementPlanes @("Browser") to create a browser-plane DLP policy.
claims.quote: The EnforcementPlanes parameter defines the layer where policy actions are run. ... -EnforcementPlanes @("<Value>") ... Browser: For use with policies applied to unmanaged cloud apps in Edge for Business.

claims.claim: The printed command creates the browser-plane policy but does not itself specify scope, rules or actions.
claims.quote: Use the New-DlpCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create data loss prevention (DLP) policies ... DLP policies contain DLP rules that identify, monitor, and protect sensitive information.

claims.claim: The policy-creation Learn scenario is hypothetical.
claims.quote: This article presents a hypothetical scenario with hypothetical values. It's only for illustrative purposes.

claims.claim: Manual resync is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Edge > Monitoring > Microsoft Purview DLP protections > Sync now.
claims.quote: Sign into the Microsoft Admin center ... Navigate to Settings > Edge > Monitoring ... On the Microsoft Purview DLP protections card, select Sync now

claims.claim: Resync does not create or update policies or groups for which the administrator lacks permissions.
claims.quote: The resync action won't create or update the policies or groups where the Admin doesn't have the required permissions.

claims.claim: An automation call for the Purview DLP protections manual resync is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Edge Purview DLP protections Sync now resync API PowerShell Microsoft Graph; Microsoft Graph Edge management Purview DLP protections resync sync now API. Read microsoft-edge-dlp-purview-configuration and Graph data security API excerpts; no matching resync operation.
